title: Generating Bayesian Network Models from Data Using Tsetlin Machines
new_feature: Uses TM global feature-strength indicators (clause weights x literal frequencies) obtained by training one TM per variable as target to propose parent/child candidates, then a search with lower-strength-direction pruning and cycle removal to build a Bayesian network DAG.

datasets.input_shape_or_features: 8 nodes (standard Asia BN; node count not stated in paper)
datasets.split_as_reported: 10 data sets sampled from the ground-truth network; sample size per data set not stated
datasets.notes: Data simulated from the bnlearn Asia network; ground-truth DAG used for graph-kernel similarity.

datasets.input_shape_or_features: 20 nodes (standard Child BN; node count not stated in paper)
datasets.split_as_reported: 10 data sets sampled from the ground-truth network; sample size not stated
datasets.notes: Data simulated from the bnlearn Child network.

datasets.split_as_reported: Sec. V: 5000 independent samples simulated from the joint distribution; per-variable balanced training subsets; Sec. V-A: 10 data sets sampled per network
datasets.booleanization: thermometer-style literals per categorical level (e.g. low/medium/high -> 100/110/111)

datasets.split_as_reported: 10 data sets sampled from the ground-truth network; sample size not stated

datasets.name_in_paper: Supply chain data set (Fashion and Beauty startup, Singh 2023)
datasets.split_as_reported: all 100 observations (one per product); no ground truth
datasets.booleanization: continuous variables discretized to low/medium/high/very high; categorical variables ranked by frequency
datasets.notes: Kaggle 'Supply Chain Analysis' (Harsh Singh 2023); URL not given in paper. Qualitative evaluation only.

datasets.booleanization: not stated (presumably as for supply chain)
datasets.notes: Public Kaggle-style churn data set (features incl. Complain, Satisfaction Score, Card Type, Point Earned), but source/URL not given in paper. Qualitative evaluation only.

extraction_notes: Only quantitative results are Table IV graph-kernel similarity scores (0-1, normalized) vs ground-truth for 4 bnlearn networks under 5 random TM parameterizations; no baselines (e.g. hill-climbing, PC) reported. Supply chain and bank churn are qualitative (top-feature tables, network figures). Node counts for Asia/Child are standard bnlearn values, not stated in paper. Split 'train' used because structure is learned on the full sampled data. No PDF rendering available; tables read from clean text.
